requirements.evidence: Both routes are registered inside the entity group (routes/web.php:56-59); Queues implements mount create auth, list, create/rename/toggle/access with every contract member (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:213-375); Serve implements scoped selection, mode-filtered 30-ticket list, all notices, locked lastCalledTicketId and 10/min rate limiting (app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:460-512); members tabs with constrained setActiveTab (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:106-124); all required lang keys in both locales (lang/en/ui.php:608-657, lang/pt_BR/ui.php:663-712).

conventions.evidence: Writes delegate to CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:240,305,341,366,374), #[Validate]/#[Locked] are used, Blade x-label/x-input components and Bulma markup match siblings, and CHANGELOG/docs/business-rules are updated (CHANGELOG.md:93-94, docs/business-rules.md:595). Deviations: per-row role/flag logic in @php and duplicated buttons in the view (resources/views/livewire/entity/queues.blade.php:952-977), dangling aria-controls in the tab bar (resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:742-750).

security.evidence: Every client id is re-resolved scoped to the entity (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:255,279,298,323,337,348,363,371; app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:481,518); server-side authorization on mount and each mutating action plus Gate::allows('call') before tickets (app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:520-524); #[Locked] entity/lastCalledTicketId; no raw output, all {{ }} escaping; no secrets or mass assignment.

tests.evidence: Substantial feature coverage: QueuesTest (292 lines) covers create/duplicate slug, rename/slug, toggle, access grant/revoke, foreign ids and accessQueueId tampering; ServeTest (267 lines) covers selection, ordering, caps, notices, 403, foreign ids and rate limiting; MembersTabsTest covers the three tab cases. Missing: unauthorized-call tests for the Queues write actions and a non-member serve test (tests/Feature/Entity/QueuesTest.php:1240-1259, tests/Feature/Entity/ServeTest.php:1542-1560).

simplicity.evidence: Reuses the existing actions, policy and x-label/x-input components rather than new layers; no speculative abstractions. Some duplication: Serve passes the same collections twice under different keys (app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:527-533) and the revoke button markup is repeated (resources/views/livewire/entity/queues.blade.php:965-972).

readability.evidence: Small, clearly named component methods and consistent sibling markup (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:219-375); however the 212-line queues view carries derivation logic and duplicated branches (resources/views/livewire/entity/queues.blade.php:952-977) and Serve has dead/aliased view data (app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:527-533).

scope.evidence: The feature files all serve the task, plus legitimate CHANGELOG/doc/lang/nav/test updates. Two entirely unrelated CI files are introduced: .github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml:1-48 and .github/workflows/tests.yml:1-24.

issues.explanation: Two new CI/deploy pipelines, including a deploy-time skip_tests escape hatch, are unrelated to the queue/serve UI task and should be split into their own change or removed.

Only the mount is tested as forbidden for employees; there is no unauthorized-call test for create, rename, toggleActive, openAccess, grantAccess or revokeAccess, which the Livewire policy requires for every action.
No test asserts that a non-member is forbidden from the serve route/component (the mount `view` authorization), even though that is a stated requirement.
assertViewHas('accessQueue', null) only checks that the key exists, so the tamper test does not actually verify that accessQueue is null and discloses nothing.
The tab buttons reference aria-controls ids members-panel/invites-panel that do not exist, and the panels have no role="tabpanel", so the tab pattern is invalid for assistive technology.
Membership role/flag derivation and the identical revoke button are embedded in a @php block and duplicated branches instead of keeping view logic out of Blade.
The view receives the same data under two names ('callableQueues'/'queues', 'tickets'/'waitingTickets') and an unused 'selectedQueue', adding dead surface.
sendInvite() now silently switches the active tab, an unrequested behavior change that ships without a test.
The comment says activeTab is constrained to a known set, but as a plain public property it can be written directly, bypassing setActiveTab(); impact is limited to which sections render.
Opening rename or access leaves viewingQueueId set, so two Bulma modals are rendered active simultaneously instead of closing the detail modal first.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues and Serve Livewire panels with their routes, navbar entries, pt_BR/en copy, members tabs and broad Pest coverage; the domain rules stay in the existing actions and every client-supplied id is re-resolved within the current entity, so the core feature and security posture are solid. It loses points for two unrelated CI/deploy workflow files and for missing the convention-mandated unauthorized-call tests on the queue write actions, with smaller issues in view logic and accessibility markup.
